newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: VICTORIA SAYS TO CUT DOMESTIC GAS PRICE FROM 1999.
newsitem.headline: VICTORIA SAYS TO CUT DOMESTIC GAS PRICE FROM 1999.

text.p: The Victorian state government said on Friday it would peg domestic gas price rises below inflation from 1999 until 2001 as a part of gas industry reform.

In a statement the government said in the three years 1999 through to the end of 2001, the price would be set at the consumer price index (CPI) rate less 2.2 percent between June to September in each of the years and CPI minus 7.7 percent for the remaining eight months of those years.
Currently, Victorian domestic gas price rises are pegged at the annual CPI rate last calculated on June 30 at 1.3 percent. This rate would be retained until December 31, 1998.

"In total, the new tariff arrangements are expected to see Victorian gas consumers paying A$1.5 billion less than if gas prices had risen in line with inflation," the Victorian government said in a statement.

Last month the Victorian government restructured its gas retail and distribution operation into six new gas companies, three retailers and three distributors as a part of its plan to maximise competition within the gas industry.
The three retailers, Kinetic Energy, Energy 21 and Ikon Energy had been allocated customers in separate geographical areas and would be privatised in 1998.
Bulk gas consumers will be able to choose between suppliers from September 1998 while household users would be given this option in September 2001.

The Victorian government said the independent Office of the Regulator General (ORG) would monitor retail prices in the transitional period from November this year while the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) would regulate the transmission of gas.
An independent ombudsman would also be appointed to provide a mechanism to resolve diputes, the government said.
